scope: Characterize the equipment opcode family for FFXIV 1.23b: SetActorAppearance (0x00D6), the inventory/equip subsystem (0x0146..0x0156, 0x016D..0x016E, 0x018E..0x0191), c2s 0x0131 UpdateItemPackage, and the corrected event-family role of c2s 0x012E, using the existing data_dependency_catalog, receiver_opcode_map_inbound, and FUN_004DC690 dispatcher map.

method.step4_dispatcher_trace: Read fun_004dc690_decomp.txt (the central s2c dispatcher). High-branch (uVar2 > 0x13D) has dedicated cases for 0x146 (FUN_005764C0), 0x148 (00576560), 0x149 (005765D0), 0x14A (00576640), 0x14B (005766B0), 0x14C (00576720), 0x14D (00576790), 0x14E (00576800), 0x14F (00576870), 0x150 (005768E0), 0x151 (00576950), 0x152 (005769C0), 0x153 (00576A30), 0x154 (00576AA0), 0x155 (00576B10), 0x156 (00576B80), 0x16D (005763C0), 0x16E (00576430). The handlers are thin wrappers: each does `uVar2 = FUN_00cc9320(*param_1); FUN_0076XXXX(uVar2, param_2)` - they obtain a per-packet context then call the per-opcode deeper handler. 0x147 InventorySetEnd is NOT in the case list (the unmapped-payload-decoding pass batch 1 noted this - Pattern E unrouted/missing). 0x00D6 SetActorAppearance is in the LOW branch (uVar2 < 0x12E) and falls through to the multi-case generic actor label (switchD_004dc749_caseD_f) which dispatches via actor->vftable[9](zone_state) - but the actor-vtable9-bulk pass exhaustively proved no actor class implements that as a real packet handler.

opcodes.wire_note: The wire layout is `entry[i] { uint32 slot; uint32 value; }` with up to 32 entries plus a u32 numEntries field at payload+0x100.

BCS-S-0014 MapInventoryTransaction remains flagged for live reverification and must not be treated as a confirmed equipment request.

The unmapped-payload-decoding pass (batch 1) also noted no case identified. Pattern E - unrouted/missing-from-client. Suggests retail-only opcode or a code path not reachable in 1.23b shipped client.

rtti_classes.note: No dedicated *EquipReceiver / *AppearanceReceiver / *InventoryReceiver RTTI classes exist in the binary - confirmed by grepping symbols.json for InventoryListX/LinkedItemList/InventorySetBegin/InventorySetEnd/InventoryBegin/InventoryEnd/InventoryItemEnd/InventoryItemPacket/InventoryRemove/SetActorAppearance/SetInitialEquipment/EquipChange/AppearanceChange and finding zero hits. This is consistent with the architectural pattern: equipment opcodes use direct-handler dispatch (Pattern C in client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns') via FUN_004DC690 high-switch dedicated cases, NOT the *Receiver class system (Pattern A used for opcodes 0x12E..0x1F5).
rtti_classes.related_struct_pending_reverify: BCS-S-0014 MapInventoryTransaction conflicts with the FUN_0075E670 / BCS-Y-0981 EventUpdatePacket builder and is flagged for live reverification.

low_branch_appearance.verdict_vtable9_dispatch: BCS-Y-0622 identifies CharaElement::vftable[9] FUN_0058CCA0 cases 0xD6 and 0xD7 as the SetActorAppearance handler. The shared helper stores indexed values at this+0xaac and sets this+0xb20=1. The actor-vtable9-bulk plurality result applies to other cataloged actor classes and does not negate the CharaElement implementation.
low_branch_appearance.implication: Static analysis closes the packet landing path through CharaElement::vftable[9]. The downstream repaint triggered from this+0xb20 remains to be characterized.

high_branch_inventory_equip.handler_pattern: Each case is `FUN_005763XX(&param_2, iVar8 + 0x10); ExceptionList = local_1c; return;` where iVar8 + 0x10 is the packet payload pointer past the 16-byte game-message header.
high_branch_inventory_equip.wrapper_pattern: Each FUN_005763XX wrapper is a 109-byte stub that: (1) calls FUN_00CC9320(*param_1) to obtain a per-packet allocation context, (2) calls the deep handler FUN_0076XXXX(uVar2, param_2) with the obtained context plus packet payload, (3) calls FUN_00CC9330 to release the context. The deep handlers (e.g. FUN_00581170 for opcode 0x14E, FUN_0076BAD0 for 0x16D) actually parse the payload and update the inventory state.

high_branch_mass_modifier.0x018E: case 0x18e not in dispatcher case list - Pattern E unrouted

data_flow_summary.c2s_player_equip_initiation: Unresolved. FUN_0075E670 / BCS-Y-0981 identifies c2s 0x012E as the generic EventUpdatePacket, not a confirmed equipment-specific transaction.
data_flow_summary.s2c_inventory_frame: The observed inventory mutation frame is 0x016D InventoryBeginChange -> 0x0146 InventorySetBegin (with ItemPackage code) -> 0x0148/9/A/B/C InventoryListX0N (item rows) and/or 0x014D-0x0151 LinkedItemListX0N (slot bindings) -> 0x0147 InventorySetEnd (the 1.23b client lacks a dispatcher case) -> 0x016E InventoryEndChange. The four gear captures contain no 0x018F, 0x0190, or 0x0191 stream, so those opcodes are not synthesized into this frame.
data_flow_summary.s2c_appearance_resend: PCAP evidence records 199 s2c 0x00D6 SetActorAppearance packets. BCS-Y-0622 identifies CharaElement::vftable[9] FUN_0058CCA0 cases 0xD6 and 0xD7 as the receive path and this+0xaac as the landing array.
data_flow_summary.request_resend_path: If client desyncs, it can request a full inventory resync via c2s 0x0131 UpdateItemPackagePacket (actorID + packageId u32 pair); the inventory-frame sequence above follows.

key_findings.title: Equipment opcodes use the dedicated-case-handler dispatch pattern (Pattern C), NOT the *Receiver class pattern (Pattern A)
key_findings.detail: Of the 24 equipment/inventory s2c opcodes (0x0146..0x0156, 0x016D, 0x016E, 0x018F, 0x0190, 0x0191), 23 have dedicated handler thunks in FUN_004DC690's high-switch (uVar2 > 0x13D) and 1 (0x0147 InventorySetEnd) is unrouted. None use the *Receiver class system used by event/social/group opcodes (Pattern A). This is consistent with the s2c dispatch architecture client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns': equipment is high-frequency inventory state that needs a tight 109-byte SEH-wrapped thunk (Pattern C) rather than the heavier per-class polymorphic dispatch.
key_findings.implication: The receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json catalog will NEVER list these opcodes - they don't fit that schema. The data_dependency_catalog.json (already covering 0x0146, 0x0148, 0x0149, 0x014E, 0x016D, 0x016E) is the correct home. The remaining 17 dispatcher thunks (BCS-Y-0586..0600) need similar entries with payload-shape decomp from the deep handlers FUN_0076XXXX.

key_findings.title: SetActorAppearance (0x00D6) lands through CharaElement::vftable[9]
key_findings.detail: BCS-Y-0622 identifies FUN_0058CCA0 cases 0xD6 and 0xD7 as the SetActorAppearance handler. The shared helper writes indexed values to this+0xaac and sets this+0xb20=1. The actor-vtable9-bulk plurality result describes other cataloged actor classes, not the CharaElement implementation.
key_findings.implication: The packet landing array is known. The remaining static-analysis question is which downstream path consumes the this+0xb20 dirty flag to repaint equipment.

key_findings.title: Opcode 0x0147 InventorySetEnd is unrouted in the v1.23b client dispatcher (Pattern E)
key_findings.detail: FUN_004DC690's high-switch case list (verified by reading fun_004dc690_decomp.txt lines 240-430) has cases for 0x146, 0x148-0x156, 0x16D, 0x16E but NO case for 0x147. unmapped_payload_decoding.json batch 1 also flagged this gap. PCAP evidence shows 84 hits for 0x147 across 53 captures (more than 0x146's 78), while the client silently drops it. This is consistent with the InventoryEndChange/SetEnd having essentially zero client-side work (a sentinel marker the client doesn't need to acknowledge).
key_findings.implication: Open question for Pattern E catalog: 0x0147 joins 0x00D2 as a known-unrouted opcode in 1.23b. Could be a retail-only addition or simply a wire artifact the client doesn't need.

key_findings.title: Observed equipment/inventory frame excludes the 0x018F-0x0191 cluster
key_findings.detail: The supported frame is BeginChange -> SetBegin -> {ItemList | LinkedItemList} -> SetEnd -> EndChange. The body, helm, soul, and weapon captures contain no 0x018F, 0x0190, or 0x0191 stream, so the prior inserted ModifierFrame step is discarded.
key_findings.implication: Do not require or synthesize the 0x018F-0x0191 cluster inside gear-change frames. Its independent transaction context remains unresolved.

key_findings.title: The c2s equipment-initiation carrier remains unresolved
key_findings.detail: FUN_0075E670 / BCS-Y-0981 confirms c2s 0x012E as the generic EventUpdatePacket with a 0x68-byte body. The BCS-S-0014 MapInventoryTransaction attribution conflicts with that first-party builder evidence.
key_findings.implication: Do not use BCS-S-0014 as a confirmed equipment request until the retail 1.23b client accepts the event-family payload during an equip action in a live session.
key_findings.reverifyMethod: live-validation against the retail 1.23b client in a live session

open_questions: Which downstream path consumes the SetActorAppearance landing array at CharaElement+0xaac after FUN_0058CCA0 cases 0xD6/0xD7 set the dirty flag at this+0xb20?

What are the deep handlers (FUN_0076XXXX) for opcodes 0x014A, 0x014B, 0x014C, 0x014D, 0x014F, 0x0150, 0x0151, 0x0152..0x0156, 0x018F, 0x0190, 0x0191? data_dependency_catalog.json only covers 6 of the 24 opcodes; 17 remain with structural-only attribution in BCS-Y-0586..0600 above.
Is opcode 0x0147 InventorySetEnd truly unused by the 1.23b client, or does it route via a non-dispatcher path? 84 pcap hits confirm repeated wire emission.

What is the exact field layout of LinkedItemEntry (in the 6-byte form)? data_dependency_catalog.json documents linkedItemPackageSlot / itemPackageSlot / itemPackageCode (all u16); acceptance by the retail 1.23b client in a live session must confirm the interpretation.
Which EventUpdate event name and Lua-parameter shape carry an equipment action over c2s 0x012E?
